title: Premature Message Queue for Low-Concurrency Internal Workloads
pattern: Introducing a heavy, broker-backed message queue (like RabbitMQ or Kafka) to communicate asynchronously between internal application components.
why_bad: External brokers introduce massive network round-trip overhead, serialization costs (JSON or Protobuf), disk write bottlenecks, and complex failure modes compared to simple in-memory channel passing or thread pool tasks [211, 422].
detection: The installation and configuration of an external message broker service to queue tasks between components running inside the same physical process or small cluster.
counterexample: Massive microservice architectures where hundreds of independent services need to distribute and process millions of async tasks. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Use standard in-memory multi-producer single-consumer channels (`std::sync::mpsc`) or thread pools (`tokio::spawn`) for safe, extremely fast, in-memory async processing.
source: *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, Chapter 10 (p. 211); *Release It!*, Section 10 (p. 422).
